mathgap.title: Sequential processing of transfers
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately adjust both the giver's and receiver's counts before processing subsequent statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form "X gives K items to Y" is encountered.
mathgap.example: Updating only the receiver's count and leaving the giver unchanged.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form "the number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have" into the equation (A − B) = (C − D). Preserve the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement equates one signed difference to another signed difference.
mathgap.example: Treating the statement as an absolute difference |A‑B| = |C‑D|.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count (e.g., "X has N items"), set X's current count to N at that moment; later statements refer to this updated value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a plain count is stated.
mathgap.example: Assuming the given count is only a starting value and later ignoring it when other statements refer to the same person.

mathgap.title: Update both parties in a transfer
mathgap.principle: For a transfer "X gives K items to Y", subtract K from X's current count and add K to Y's current count in the same step.
mathgap.example: Adding K to Y but forgetting to subtract K from X.

mathgap.title: Systematic linear solving
mathgap.principle: Collect all algebraic constraints (counts, differences, sums, etc.) into a system of linear equations and solve it by substitution or elimination, ensuring consistency.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After all statements have been translated into equations.
mathgap.example: Leaving a set of equations unsolved and guessing a value for the target variable.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All derived counts must be non‑negative integers; if an equation yields a negative or fractional value, the current interpretation is wrong.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the linear system or when a new value is computed.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person ends up with –3 items.

mathgap.title: Split operation handling
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among two recipients, set the giver's count to zero and give each recipient half of the original amount (the total must be even).
mathgap.when_to_apply: For statements like "X splits all the items she owns equally among A and B".
mathgap.example: Leaving the giver with the original amount and only adding half to each recipient.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form "If X has more than N items, X will transfer their items to Y", first evaluate X's current count; if it exceeds N, move all of X's items to Y (set X to 0 and add the transferred amount to Y). Otherwise, do nothing.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a conditional transfer clause with a numeric threshold.
mathgap.example: Treating the conditional as an unconditional transfer and moving X's items regardless of the threshold.

mathgap.title: Redistribution equalization handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X and Y redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount", pool their current counts, compute the total, and set each of X and Y to total / 2 (the problem guarantees the total is even).
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any "redistribute ... to ensure each has an equal amount" clause involving two persons.
mathgap.example: Giving each person half of their own original count instead of half of the combined total.

mathgap.title: Combined statements handling
mathgap.principle: Interpret any statement that involves a sum of multiple persons on one side as a linear equation: • For "X has N more items than Y and Z combined", write X = Y + Z + N (or X − (Y+Z) = N). • For "The combined quantity of X, Y, Z is N", write X + Y + Z = N. This also covers simple comparisons as a special case where the sum contains a single term.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement mentions two or more persons together on one side, either as a combined quantity or as a combined comparison.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "X has N more items than Y and Z combined" as X = Y + N, ignoring Z.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the sign and uses |A‑B| instead of A‑B, losing directionality.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of names; translate "A has more than B" to A = B + N, not |A‑B| = N.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats all transfers as simultaneous, missing updates that affect later statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer in the order presented, updating counts before the next statement.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a given count as immutable, forgetting that later transfers can change it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct count assignments as the current value at that point; allow later statements to modify it.

mathgap.description: Updating only the receiver in a transfer
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model adds the transferred amount to the receiver but forgets to subtract it from the giver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When processing a transfer, adjust both parties: subtract from the giver, add to the receiver.

mathgap.description: Reversing the direction in "X has N more than Y" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model swaps the subjects, writing X = Y − N instead of X = Y + N.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Maintain the order: "X has N more than Y" means X = Y + N; "X has N fewer than Y" means X = Y − N.
